newsitem.title: CANADA: Imperial Oil, union labor talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Imperial Oil, union labor talks continue.

text.p: Officials at Imperial Oil Ltd and the union representing 160 workers at the company's 112,000 barrel per day Nanticoke, Ontario refinery were negotiating on Monday after a weekend of talks aimed at hammering out a labor deal, a company official said.

The workers have given a strike mandate to their Canadian Energy and Paperworkers union bargaining committee, although no deadline for a strike had been set by Monday, said assistant refinery manager Paddy Roach.

Roach declined to outline the major issues that were keeping the sides from reaching a collective agreement, which would be the workers' first since they voted in favor of CEP representation last January.

"The bargaining is going on right at this time and I think it would be inappropriate for me to comment on that. We're attempting to keep the negotiating at the table," Roach said. "We are optimistic that an agreement will be reached."
He said the company planned to continue the operation of the refinery in the event of a strike with workers from the refinery as well as others from other company plants.
"Our plan is to continue to operate the plant normally and we don't anticipate any impact on our customers," Roach said.
Union officials were not immediately available for comment.
The plant at Nanticoke, located about 100 km southwest of Toronto, is Imperial's third-largest refinery. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
